source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"It treats established HPV infection and removes existing lesions after an abnormal screening result.","B":"It prevents new infections with vaccine HPV types and works best when given before exposure.","C":"It should be started only after sexual activity begins so prior exposure can stimulate vaccine response.","D":"It removes the need for recommended cervical screening because vaccination prevents every oncogenic HPV type."}}
source_row.rationale: HPV vaccination prevents new HPV infections and is most effective before exposure. It does not treat established infection or existing lesions and does not eliminate recommended screening. Option B is correct. C incorrectly delays vaccination until after exposure is more likely.
source_row.source_detail: HPV vaccination guidance: vaccination prevents new HPV infections and works best before exposure; it does not treat existing HPV infection or disease. Routine vaccination is recommended at ages 11-12 (can start at 9), with catch-up through age 26 if not adequately vaccinated. Current CDC HPV vaccine recommendations live-rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Health Promotion and Maintenance: preventive screening, immunization, pregnancy/reproductive health and age/risk-appropriate teaching activities as applicable. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
